name: Ironveil Chrome-Scrap Street Set
description: This outfit is where Shelf survival meets the aesthetic of the aug-yards — the salvage zones where stripped chrome and discarded cyberware get broken down for parts. The wearer has built their look around that world deliberately. A close-fitting long-sleeve shirt in dark graphite, made from a heavy thermal weave with aug-channel seams running along both arms — the channels are empty, not functional, but the shirt was built for chrome-users and found its way down to the Shelf. Over it hangs a sleeveless vest constructed from layered strips of salvaged materials: sections of conveyor belt rubber, cut canvas, pieces of what was once a ballistic panel, all stitched and riveted together into a rough asymmetric armor-vest that sits heavier on the left side. Salvaged chrome components — a single non-functional forearm housing stripped of its internals, worn as a bracer on the right arm; a defunct sensor ring worn as a thick wrist cuff on the left — accessorize without augmenting, a visual claim on a world that's financially out of reach. Straight-leg trousers in charcoal industrial denim, the right knee blown out and re-patched with black rubber, are tucked into mid-calf lace-up boots with thick composite soles, the leather upper cracked and re-treated until it's almost matte black. A close-cropped knit beanie in faded black, hand-stitched with a small geometric pattern in rust thread at the cuff, sits low over the ears.
materials: heavy thermal weave with aug-channel seams
functionality: Aug-channel shirt accommodates functional chrome arms if the wearer ever acquires them. Layered vest provides moderate impact and abrasion protection. Salvaged chrome bracer protects the forearm from debris and light strikes despite being non-functional internally. Composite-soled boots provide grip and durability on industrial terrain.
what_it_says: This person knows the aug world from the outside — close enough to scavenge its castoffs, far enough away to never afford entry. The chrome accessories are aspirational and confrontational at once, a refusal to be invisible. The hand-stitched beanie is the one thing that's entirely theirs.
worn_by: anyone who moves between the aug trade and the street
manufacturer: Shirt is a Pragma Systems aug-compatible base layer, heavily worn; vest is fully self-constructed; chrome accessories are stripped aug-yard salvage
price_range: Φ20–Φ45 depending on chrome scrap value
story_hooks: One of the salvaged chrome pieces isn't as non-functional as the wearer believes — a faint signal is still broadcasting from the sensor ring, and someone is tracking it.
A Tier 4 chrome-surgeon notices the aug-channel shirt and offers a deal: functional installation of salvaged chrome in exchange for a favor that sounds too easy.
The geometric pattern on the beanie is a territorial marker from a Shelf crew that no longer exists — and an older resident recognizes it, with complicated feelings.
